newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends up, shuns optimistic EPA report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends up, shuns optimistic EPA report.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen futures contract ended firmer on Friday, ignoring a monthly economic report by Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) that showed a brighter view on the economy, traders said.

The EPA said that Japan's economy was firming up and that the EPA's assessment of the Japanese economy was half-a-step more optimistic than last month. The March moved in 99.02-06 range, compared with 98.99-02 range for Thursday.
The market remained focused on the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) allegedly bearish view of the economy, traders said.
Some BOJ officials appear to be telling the market that the central bank would be unable to raise interest rates in the current fiscal year ending March 31, 1998, they said.
"In terms of economic fundamentals, it is high time the BOJ tightened its credit grip," said a European bank trader.

However, as for the health of Japanese banking sector, its bad-loan woes are far from being over as financial troubles at regional banks, brokerages and construction companies have just started surfacing, he added.
"The market has recently failed to respond to economic data showing a healthy recovery because traders are sensing the BOJ's lingering pessimism over the economy," said a city bank trader.
The BOJ's pessimism is partly due to the slow pace of recovery in businesses of small enterprises as the current recovery is led by major exporting manufacturers, he added.

In the interest rate swap market (IRS), a major city bank received fixed interest rates intermittently, adding to bullish sentiment, traders said. The three-year IRS was quoted at 1.39/43 percent, unchanged from late Thursday.
The central bank injected 100 billion yen into the money market via its regular market operation at 0020 GMT, fully offseting a projected shortfall of 100 billion yen.
The benchmark overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
The market is waiting for BOJ's regional governors' meeting on July 14-15 to provide a clue to market direction.
The March's near-term support is at 98.95 and the major resistance lies at 99.15, traders said.
